question.text: In the SEBI-prescribed PPM template, what is the key difference between Section VIII for a Category I/II AIF versus a Category III AIF?

answer.text: Cat I/II Section VIII covers 'Principles of Portfolio Valuation' while Cat III Section VIII covers 'Determination of the Net Asset Value of Units' — reflecting illiquid valuation vs NAV-based valuation
Cat I/II Section VIII is about tax treatment while Cat III is about leverage
Section VIII is identical for both; the difference is only in Section IX
Cat I/II don't have a Section VIII at all

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the PPM template structure in Section 13.5, Section VIII for Category I/II AIFs is titled 'Principles of Portfolio Valuation', while Section VIII for Category III AIFs is titled 'Determination of the Net Asset Value of Units'. The two sections cover different valuation mechanics aligned to each category's portfolio characteristics. The Trap: Tax treatment and leverage are dealt with under separate PPM sections, not Section VIII. Section VIII is not identical across categories — the title and content differ. Category I/II do have a Section VIII; it is just titled and scoped differently from the Category III version. Note: The category-by-category split of Section VIII is the precise point being tested: 'Principles of Portfolio Valuation' for Cat I/II versus 'Determination of the Net Asset Value of Units' for Cat III.
